Title: Review: Code review on your own machine, with optional AI | Product Hunt
# Review. ## Code review on your own machine, with optional AI. A desktop app for Git branches and GitHub pull requests. Comment on any line, publish when you're ready, and add an AI reviewer with your own model, or none. Launch tags:Open Source•Developer Tools•Artificial Intelligence. I'm Hamed, and I made Review. I'm a developer and team lead. Since AI started writing so much of our code, reviewing it all has become the hardest part of my job. So I built Review: a desktop app for reviewing pull requests, where you can set up a team of AI reviewers from different providers to take the first pass. You still decide what gets published. - Opens your local Git branches and GitHub pull requests in one window. ⌘P jumps to any of them. - Pins each review to exact commits, so the diff doesn't shift when someone pushes. - Keeps your comments on your machine until you publish them to GitHub as a review. - Adds an AI reviewer if you want one: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, or a local model in Ollama or LM Studio. Your keys are stored in the system keychain. **What's different about the AI part**: it checks every change against a fixed set of rules (bugs, security, error handling, tests and more), and it shows which rules it actually checked, not just what it found. If a request fails, you can retry only the rules it missed. It can also call your MCP servers for context the code doesn't have, like the ticket behind a change. It's free, open source (MIT) and needs no account. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux. One heads-up: the installers aren't signed yet, so your system will ask once the first time you open it. The website has the two-click fix. I'd love to know: what's the most annoying part of code review for you today? And which model would you plug in first? See what products Review uses for development, design, marketing, analytics, and more. Electron FiddleCreate, run, package, and share experiments with Electron. Electron let me ship Review as a real desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux from one codebase, with access to Git, the file system and the system keychain. OllamaThe easiest way to run large language models locally. Ollama is how Review offers fully local AI code review. Pick a model, and your code never leaves your machine. Its OpenAI-compatible API made the integration straightforward. Claude by AnthropicA family of foundational AI models. Built much of Review with Claude Code: from the AI review runner to the retry and stop/resume flow. It handled the whole loop, from code and tests to PRs and the release, and kept the codebase consistent as it grew.
